name: Boro Softstep

texts.0: Come to learn how a Hunter plays Hearthstone? I begin with companions. Nali says I take a long time to begin.
texts.1: Uncle Boro can describe a companion for an hour. He can describe why he would not choose it for two.
texts.2: We have not finished comparing companions. Shall I go on?
texts.3: Nali is nearby. Let us find out what all this was supposed to accomplish.
texts.5: What did Nali actually ask for? I would rather hear her words than another of my splendid ideas.
texts.6: No more speeches about companions. I have brought the cards.
texts.7: Nali says I am allowed to explain my choices after I have made them. This seems fair. Shall we play?
texts.8: You won fairly. Your Hunter Deck is ready. I have no further questions about animals.
texts.9: Good to see you, $n. Nali has started asking me what my lessons are for. I may have taught her rather too well.
texts.10: He finally played. I still like the boar. I like Uncle Boro better when he stops examining everyone.
texts.11: He has stopped comparing companions. Now I might finally see the cards.
texts.12: I have lost my place. Let us consider those three again.
texts.13: It is easy to get carried away. Shall we start that part again?
texts.14: Has he reached the accountant? Then you have been here a while.
texts.15: I asked to see how he plays his Hunter deck. One game. He said we had to choose the proper companion first.
texts.16: I chose the boar. He said it was wrong. Then he put a boar in his own deck and said that was different. I would like him to show me the difference by playing.
texts.17: Thank you. If he starts another examination, tell him the boar has already passed mine.
texts.18: Well? A grand hunt? A tiger?
texts.19: One game. I could have managed that without the accountant.
texts.20: Yes. I have been telling her what a Hunter should notice while missing the person standing beside me. No more auditions.
texts.21: A bear, a buzzard and a tiger. Which would you choose?
texts.22: Wrong. The bear would take you. It would decide you were carrying lunch.
texts.23: Wrong. It waits for you to die before becoming helpful. I prefer a companion with a little more urgency.
texts.24: Wrong. A magnificent hunter, but it expects the finest cut of everything. Including your blanket.
texts.25: A wolf, a boar and a turtle. More modest appetites. Mostly. Which one?
texts.26: Wrong. It howls when it finds something. By the time it has finished announcing breakfast, breakfast has left.
texts.27: Wrong. It is very good at finding things underground. I was hoping to keep most of the ground where it is.
texts.28: Wrong. An excellent companion for yesterday's hunt. We would arrive next week.
texts.29: A frog, a chicken and a tauren accountant. Keep an open mind. The accountant is very good at following people.
texts.30: Wrong. It could catch a fly, but I doubt it would share.
texts.31: Wrong. The chicken would be the bait. I do not like its chances.
texts.32: Wrong. He finds every copper you have ever earned, then charges you for the discovery.
texts.4: That is a fair question. Nali asked me for a lesson. Somewhere between the bear and the accountant, I stopped asking what she wanted to learn.
texts.33: Listen carefully. We shall consider them one at a time.
texts.34: One lesson at a time. Even I must finish a sentence eventually.

quests.Title: A Fine Selection
quests.Details: My niece Nali asked for a Hunter lesson. A good lesson begins with a useful companion. I have given the matter considerable thought. $B$BI will describe a few candidates. Tell me which one you would choose. There is more to a companion than teeth, though I find teeth are a reliable place to begin.
quests.RequestItemsText: We still have a set to consider. I assure you, the next one is entirely reasonable.
quests.OfferRewardText: Hm. We have learned a great deal about me and rather less about what Nali needs.$B$BPerhaps we should correct that.

quests.Title: What She Asked For
quests.Details: Nali is here on Hunter Rise, probably listening to the hunter trainers. She has been remarkably patient with my lesson. She may have been waiting for me to stop speaking.$B$BAsk her what she wanted when she came to me. I have had enough of listening to myself for one afternoon.
quests.Objectives: Ask Nali what she wanted from Boro's lesson, then tell Boro.
quests.RequestItemsText: What did Nali actually ask for? I would rather hear her words than another of my splendid ideas.
quests.OfferRewardText: I was choosing her companion before I had even heard her question. No wonder every answer seemed wrong.$B$BShe wanted a game. Let us give her one worth watching.

quests.Title: No More Auditions
quests.Details: Nali wanted to see how I play my Hunter deck. You have endured enough of my opinions to deserve the other side of the table.$B$BBring whichever deck you like. Defeat me, and this Hunter Deck is yours. I shall try to make my companions more useful than my questions.
quests.Objectives: Defeat Boro Softstep in a game of Hearthstone.
quests.RequestItemsText: Another game? At last, a question with a sensible answer.
quests.OfferRewardText: Well played, $n. Nali was right to ask for the game first.$B$BTake this Hunter Deck. I will not ask which animal you intend to put in it.

replies: What did you ask him to teach you?
I'll tell him you want a game.
She asked to watch you play.
Let her see how you actually play.

name: Fenn Coilwhistle

texts.0: I teach Hunter play by describing animals and asking which one a student would take. Eris, who reads her reports over there, says I do it too loudly. I think she needs a companion of her own, something quiet. I am choosing one.
texts.1: Fenn is planning another lesson. If he starts one while you are nearby, find somewhere else to sit.
texts.2: We have not finished choosing Eris's companion. Shall I go on?
texts.3: Eris is nearby in the Cenarion Enclave. Go and ask her what she needs. She is usually very precise about problems.
texts.5: What does Eris need? Keep it short. I have done enough talking this week.
texts.6: Cards make no noise at all. Eris has approved of them in principle.
texts.7: Ready? I have an ordinary Hunter deck. If I lose, that will be my own fault. Eris made me promise to say so out loud.
texts.8: You won. Your Hunter Deck is ready. Eris says it was a fair game, which surprised us both.
texts.9: Good to see you, $n. The lessons are shorter now, and Eris has stopped complaining. Mostly.
texts.10: Cards. No long speeches. I may even finish this report before he offers me a game.
texts.11: He listened. That is worth encouraging. Preferably with something that fits in his pocket.
texts.12: One moment. I have lost my place.
texts.13: Give me a moment. I have lost my train of thought.
texts.14: Please tell me he has finished talking.
texts.15: Quiet. He describes things so well that I stop reading and listen. I asked him for less talking. He has spent all week choosing me a companion instead.
texts.16: No companion. I like Fenn. I would just like to finish one report without a lesson going on beside me.
texts.17: Thank you. He is a good friend. He is also a great deal of noise for one gnome.
texts.18: Well? What does she need? Did she pick a companion?
texts.19: No companion at all? Then what if I keep my voice very low?
texts.20: All right. No more lessons at her desk. I spent a week looking for a clever answer to a question she never asked.
texts.21: First set: a cat, an owl and a spider. All quiet. Which would you bring her?
texts.22: Wrong. Quiet on its paws, but it would sit on Eris's reports. Cats always find the page that matters.
texts.23: Wrong. Silent wings, but it would watch Eris read all evening. Nobody finishes a report under that stare.
texts.24: Wrong. Quiet, yes, but Eris would find it in her papers by morning, and I would hear about it.
texts.25: Second set: a crab, a crocolisk and a rabbit. Which would you bring her?
texts.26: Wrong. Those claws click on every stone step. Eris would hear it coming from the far end of the Enclave.
texts.27: Wrong. Patient, until it is not, and then it thrashes. The Enclave is meant to be a quiet place.
texts.28: Wrong. It bolts at the smallest noise, even a page turning, and knocks something over on the way out.
texts.29: Last set: a rat, a sheep and a gnome accountant. Which would you bring her?
texts.30: Wrong. It would be inside Eris's report cabinet within the hour.
texts.31: Wrong. Calm, until it is left alone. Then it bleats, and Eris would be the one who went to see why.
texts.32: Wrong. I have costed that one. Quiet and tidy, but it would audit Eris's reports, and she would never forgive me.
texts.4: ...No. She asked for quiet, and I decided she needed company. I never asked what she actually wants. Perhaps you should.
texts.33: Pay attention. This part takes imagination.
texts.34: One lesson at a time. I have only the one pair of pointing hands.

quests.Title: A Quieter Companion
quests.Details: I give Hunter lessons out here, and my friend Eris, a Sentinel, reads her reports nearby. She says my lessons are too loud. I have decided that what she needs is a companion of her own, something quiet to keep her company, so that she will be in a better mood for my teaching.$B$BI will go through three sets of candidates. Tell me which one you would bring her from each, and remember that she needs quiet to read.
quests.Objectives: Help Fenn Coilwhistle choose a quiet companion for Eris from his three sets.
quests.RequestItemsText: Another set is ready. Surely one of them is quiet enough for Eris.
quests.OfferRewardText: I have rejected every one. You chose carefully, I will say that. The trouble is that I never checked what Eris actually wants.$B$BI should have started there.

quests.Title: Less Wildlife, Please
quests.Details: Eris is on duty in the Cenarion Enclave, though I suspect she is also trying to read her reports. I would like to know exactly what she needs.$B$BAsk her, then tell me what she said. Please do not soften it.
quests.Objectives: Ask Eris what she needs, then tell Fenn.
quests.RequestItemsText: What does Eris need? Keep it short. I have done enough talking this week.
quests.OfferRewardText: No lessons at her desk. Plain enough, isn't it?$B$BVery well. If I want Eris to take my lessons seriously, I can begin by noticing when she is trying to read.

quests.Title: Keep It on the Cards
quests.Details: Eris can read in peace now, and I have had time to think. My lessons are best when I stop trying to impress people.$B$BLet us play Hearthstone. Bring whichever deck you like. Defeat me, and this Hunter Deck is yours. Cards are much quieter than my lessons.
quests.Objectives: Defeat Fenn Coilwhistle in a game of Hearthstone.
quests.RequestItemsText: Shall we try again? I have resisted making another lesson of it.
quests.OfferRewardText: Well played, $n. My lessons improve whenever I stop trying to win people over.$B$BTake this Hunter Deck. Eris, you needn't look up. I lost.

replies: Fenn sent me. What do you need?
So you don't need a companion?
She wants to read without interruptions.
No lessons at her desk, Fenn.
